options.b: C2-b count is a separate product; form is an axis
options.c: C2-c both are separate products, no family link

cells: named explicitly as a count axis
eBay (Number in Pack, aspectEnabledForVariations true on 12/12 grocery leaves — gap pass 2026-09-21, sandbox)

subtallies.name: Restricts axis eligibility by a mechanism not about count
cells: Walmart (per product type — ten food types have no variant mechanism at all)
Akeneo (per attribute type — a count fits metric or simple select)

subtallies.name: Carries a separate pack / bundle mechanism beside variation
cells: Shopee (add_kit_item / update_kit_item / get_kit_item_info with component_list[] and its own tier_variation_list[])
Tokopedia Era B (combined_skus[] {product_id, sku_id, sku_count} on the SKU — structured spec 2026-09-21)

framing: Card correction: (a) and (b) are not alternatives on any platform that has both — Amazon and Walmart each name count as a legal axis AND carry a separate pack/bundle mechanism, because the two answer different questions (“same product in different amounts?” vs “a container for other rows?”). GS1 splits our one word into three: consumer multipack (§2.3, same level as the single, new GTIN — consumer distinguishes: YES) · case/carton (§2.8 — higher-level packaging only: NO) · predefined assortment of different products (§2.9 — own GTIN separate from the components': YES). GS1 is P1 (a member-organisation copy; the gs1.org URL 404s). The nine “expressible but unnamed” platforms did not decide anything — silence is not support for (a).

rows.h: explicitly — and (b)'s mechanism exists beside it, not instead
rows.shape: “if you set the variation_theme to SIZE/COLOR/NUMBER_OF_ITEMS, then shirt_size, color, and number_of_items become mandatory”; the legacy→JSON theme map carries count → ITEM_PACKAGE_QUANTITY; the Health workbook's valid-values list is Color · Count · SizeName · SizeName-ColorName. Separately, ItemRelationship.type is an enum of exactly two: VARIATION — “is a variation parent or variation child of the related items” — and PACKAGE_HIERARCHY — “is a package container or is contained by the related items that are identified by ASIN.” The distinction Amazon draws is containment, not count. New, first-party 2026-09-21: ItemClassification has four values — BASE_PRODUCT, OTHER, PRODUCT_BUNDLE (“A parent catalog item that represents a bundle of items”), VARIATION_PARENT — so a bundle is a classified catalogue item, a third parent kind beside the two relationship types.

rows.h: explicitly — with a separate bundle mechanism; count is its most universal axis
rows.shape: “Common variant attributes include: Color · Size · Pattern · Character · Count · Count per pack · Multipack quantity · Theme.” 6,957 product types each carry their own variantAttributeNames.items.enum, 2,323 distinct axis names, enum size 1 / 2,323 / mean 11.75; Toothpastes allows 9 = [character, character_group, count, countPerPack, flavor, form, multipackQuantity, pieceCount, size], Tires 18, and “they intersect only in count, countPerPack, multipackQuantity” — the only axes a toothpaste and a tyre share. Ten food types (Apples, Avocados, Bananas, Fresh Herbs, Grapes, Mushrooms, Onions, Packaged Salads, Pears, Watermelons) have no variant mechanism at all. Virtual Pack: bundleType=VIRTUALPACK + the component's gtin. Stated why: “display multiple versions of the same product on a single Walmart item page … vary by color, size, flavor, pattern, count.”

rows.h: expressible; the multipack is an offer attribute as well, which is orthogonal
rows.shape: [multipack] is an ordinary product attribute — Integer, example 6: “Required (for multipack products in Australia, Brazil, Czechia, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Spain, Switzerland, the UK and the US) · Optional for all other products and target countries”; [is_bundle] (yes/no) with the identical qualifier. Named variant attributes are eight — “color, size, pattern, material, age group, gender, size type and size system” — and “no artifact stating a closed set found”; every list introduced by “such as” or “like”. Inference: item_group_id exists to render a picker; multipack exists to let a comparison normalise price-per-unit — different jobs, different fields.

rows.h: closed by the gap pass 2026-09-21: Number in Pack pivots on 12 of 12 grocery leaves (sandbox)
rows.shape: Axis eligibility is per aspect: “Not all aspects are allowed as a pivoting aspect … look for a value of true in the aspectEnabledForVariations field.” Gap pass 2026-09-21, sandbox tree 0 v134, 12 grocery leaves (Noodles, Pasta & Noodles, Chips, Soft Drinks, Instant Coffee, Cookies, Chocolate Blocks, Cooking Sauces, Water, Tea, Juices, Nuts): Number in Pack is aspectEnabledForVariations: true on 12 of 12; Unit Quantity is false on 12 of 12 (aspectApplicableTo: ["ITEM"]); Number of Servings true on 6 of 12. Verbatim, leaf 257998: Number in Pack {aspectDataType: STRING, itemToAspectCardinality: SINGLE, aspectMode: FREE_TEXT, aspectRequired: false, aspectUsage: OPTIONAL, aspectEnabledForVariations: true}, no suggested values — count is a bare free-text label. Item Weight pivots with suggested values "250 g", "1 kg" — label+unit strings, never typed. Flavor pivots on 11 of 12 (5 suggested values on Noodles: Beef, Chicken, Chili, Curry, Seafood); the Pasta & Noodles leaf has no Flavor aspect at all.

ProductOption.name is free text — “"Flavor" needs no taxonomy involvement at all for an unlinked option.” Max 3 options per product. Live 2026-09-21: the taxonomy carries pack form as a choice list — Package type (1456: Bag, Bottle, Box, Can, Canister, Case, Dispenser, Flip-top, …) on Soda — and no count / pack-quantity attribute on any of 9 food nodes sampled.

rows.h: expressible, unnamed; a kit item is “a variant family the standardisation has not reached”
rows.shape: “If you want to use customized variations, then pass variation_id=0 and pass variation_name.” Kit items: add_kit_item (49 request paths) / update_kit_item / get_kit_item_info, carrying item_setting.model_list[] {tier_index, model_sku, original_price, component_list[] {component_item_id, component_model_id, quantity, main_component}} and its own free-text tier_variation_list[] — “a row that owns axes and whose members carry tier_index and their own price and SKU.”

rows.h: Era B — expressible, unnamed; cap of 3 sales attributes
rows.shape: “Provide either a built-in ID or a custom name; if both are provided, the ID takes priority.” “You can only have up to 3 types of sales attributes per product.” Structured spec 2026-09-21: a separate bundle mechanism on the SKU — combined_skus[] {product_id Y, sku_id Y, sku_count: int Y} — beside the sales-attribute axis; sku_unit_count: string.
The axis is item_options with free-text option values (CatalogItemOptionValue.name).
Variation attributes are defined per master (ProductVariationAttribute); no attribute-kind restriction retrieved.
The axis predicate is is_global == SCOPE_GLOBAL + usesSource() (a select type) + visible + user-defined; no restriction on what the attribute means.
The axis flag is one bool per attribute entry — is_variation.
Any AttributeDefinition may carry attributeConstraint: CombinationUnique — “Set of Attributes that have this constraint, should have different combinations in each variant.”

rows.h: expressible, type-gated; six vendor statements, three different answers on which types may be an axis (C3)
rows.shape: “Only the following attribute types are allowed: simple select, multi select, reference data, metric, boolean.” (the CE array names 5, the spec names 5 with different membership, the Serenity page names up to 10 incl. Number and Text). A count fits metric or simple select on every version.
